title: Pointwise etale perversities and localization of perverse extension
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and $X$ a Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Use ordinary small etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For a point $x$, put $R\Gamma_xM=i_x^!(M|_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}})$, where $i_x$ is the closed-point inclusion and $i_x^!$ is the right derived supported kernel [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its geometric fibre is computed as $R\Gamma_{\{x_0\}}(X_{(\bar x)},M|_{X_{(\bar x)}})$, with $x_0$ the closed point [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Let $p:|X|\to\mathbf Z$ be nondecreasing under specialization. The conditions
$$D^{\leq p}=\{M\in D^+:H^a(M|_{\bar x})=0\text{ for }a>p(x)\},\qquad D^{\geq p}=\{M\in D^+:H^a(R\Gamma_{\bar x}M)=0\text{ for }a<p(x)\}$$
define a t-structure [def-weil-t-structure] on $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$; here $M|_{\bar x}$ is the geometric stalk at a geometric point $\bar x$ over $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Denote its heart by $\operatorname{Perv}^p(X)$ and its upper truncation by $\tau_{\leq p}$.

A pseudo-open immersion $f:Y\to X$ means a scheme morphism inducing a homeomorphism onto its image and an isomorphism $f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_Y$. For such $f$ between Noetherian schemes, the inverse image $f^*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is t-exact for $p$ and $p\circ f$, and the derived direct image $Rf_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] preserves the lower class. The functor
$$f_*^p=\tau_{\leq p}Rf_*:\operatorname{Perv}^{p\circ f}(Y)\to\operatorname{Perv}^p(X)$$
is a fully faithful right adjoint of $f^*$, its counit $f^*f_*^p\to\mathrm{id}$ is an isomorphism, and $f_*^p g_*^{p\circ f}\cong(fg)_*^p$ for composable pseudo-open immersions. These identifications respect units and counits.

For etale restriction and for localization or strict localization, pullback is t-exact for the pulled-back function, and perverse extension from a generic point of a normal integral scheme commutes with that restriction (componentwise on the resulting normal integral components: for $h:Y\to X$, use the base-changed generic scheme $\eta_Y=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ and $j_Y:\eta_Y\to Y$; on each component it is its generic point, and $h^*j_*^p\cong j_{Y,*}^{p\circ h}h_\eta^*$). Here etale and strict localization are [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and normal integral means [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. In particular, let $X$ be local strictly henselian with closed point $x$, let $g:U=X-\{x\}\hookrightarrow X$, and let $L\in\operatorname{Perv}^{p|_U}(U)$. If $L$ is also ordinarily bounded above by $p(x)$, then
$$g_*^pL\cong\tau^{\mathrm{ord}}_{\leq p(x)}Rg_*L.$$
The ordinary truncation does not alter the restriction to $U$, and this isomorphism is compatible with the adjunction map to $Rg_*L$.

source.place: Expose XVII, 5.2, Definition 5.2.1, Proposition 5.2.2(a)-(d); etale/localization locality as in 2.2.1 and the first reduction of proof 5.3.1(a), printed pp. 287–288

proof.text: First suppose $X$ is nonempty. By [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components] and [lem-sc-scheme-sober] it has finitely many component generic points $\eta_i$. Every point specializes from some $\eta_i$, so $b=\min_i p(\eta_i)$ is a lower bound for $p$. Put $\Phi^a=\{x:p(x)\geq a\}$. The specialization inequality makes each $\Phi^a$ specialization closed; $\Phi^{a+1}\subseteq\Phi^a$ and $\Phi^a=X$ for $a\leq b$. Apply [lem-per-etale-support-aisle-generators] to this filtration and [lem-per-set-generated-sheaf-aisle] to its set of generators $G_{V,Z,a}$. Their smallness follows from the chosen small etale skeleton and the set of closed subsets of each affine object. We obtain an unbounded t-structure with upper class $\mathcal U_\Phi$ and orthogonal complement $\mathcal U_\Phi^\perp$. Its upper condition says exactly that $\mathcal H^a(K)_{\bar x}=0$ whenever $a>p(x)$. The empty scheme has zero derived category and all asserted classes and functors are zero.

source.place: XVII 5.2, existence, support-filtration construction expanded into its abstract and geometric inputs

proof.text: For bounded-below $B$, the generator test in [lem-per-set-generated-sheaf-aisle] asks for $\operatorname{Hom}(G_{V,Z,a}[k],B)=0$ for every $k\geq0$. By [lem-per-supported-generators-costalk-detection] these are precisely the groups $H^{a-k}R\Gamma_Z(V,B|_V)$; applying its equivalence to $S=\Phi^a$ gives $H^m(C_{\bar x}B)=0$ for all $m\leq a$ whenever $p(x)\geq a$. Taking $a=p(x)$ shows that $\mathcal U_\Phi^\perp\cap D^+=D^{\geq p+1}$. The unbounded triangle $A\to K\to B$ of Step 1 stays in $D^+$ when $K\in D^+$: $D^{\mathrm{ord},\leq b}\subseteq\mathcal U_\Phi$, so ordinary orthogonality implies $B\in D^{\mathrm{ord},\geq b+1}$; the cohomology sequence then bounds $A$ below by the minimum of a lower bound for $K$ and $b$. Ordinary cohomology and its orthogonality are [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], and the truncation orthogonality/triangle properties are [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. Thus the restriction is a t-structure on $D^+$, with exactly the two stated pointwise conditions. Its truncations and heart have the stated meaning.

source.place: XVII 5.2, cosupport characterization and bounded-below domain

proof.text: Let $f:Y\to X$ be pseudo-open. Its underlying map preserves specialization, so $p\circ f$ has the required inequality. Inverse image is exact on constant-coefficient modules by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], its geometric stalk at $\bar y$ is the original stalk at $f\bar y$. The strict-local-fibre comparison [lem-per-pseudo-open-strict-local-fibre] identifies the pointed strict local schemes and the restrictions of the complex there. Therefore it identifies their supported cohomology at the closed point, hence their geometric costalks, using the definition $C_{\bar x}$ in [lem-per-supported-generators-costalk-detection]. The two pointwise vanishing conditions prove t-exactness of $f^*$. To reconcile the residue-field and strict-local descriptions in the statement, apply [lem-per-ind-etale-closed-support-base-change] after localizing at the point, to the affine strict-henselization map; its ind-etale property is [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-affine-chart-ind-etale]. Taking the closed geometric fibre of that closed-support comparison is exactly $C_{\bar x}$. No excellence hypothesis is needed. The local base is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], and its strict henselization is Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian], so both Noetherian hypotheses of the closed-support comparison hold.

source.place: XVII Proposition 5.2.2(a); Definition 1.1.1 for the costalk convention

proof.text: The adjunction $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ is the bounded-below derived adjunction of [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction], applied to the exact left adjoint of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. If $L\in D^{\geq p\circ f}$ and $A\in D^{\leq p-1}$, then $\operatorname{Hom}(A,Rf_*L)=\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,L)=0$ by Step 3 and t-orthogonality. The characterization of the lower class by this orthogonality gives $Rf_*L\in D^{\geq p}$. The orthogonality characterization follows from the truncation triangle in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]: the universal map from the upper truncation of an orthogonal object is zero, forcing that upper truncation to vanish. Enough injectives on module sheaves is [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives].

For $L$ in the heart on $Y$, Step 4 puts $Rf_*L$ in the lower class. The upper truncation $T=\tau_{\leq p}Rf_*L$ also lies in that lower class by the truncation properties [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], hence lies in the heart. For $M$ in the heart on $X$, upper truncation adjunction and derived adjunction give natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(M,T)=\operatorname{Hom}(M,Rf_*L)=\operatorname{Hom}(f^*M,L)$. These define the heart adjunction and its unit and counit. In particular its map $T\to Rf_*L$ is the upper-truncation counit, and the heart counit is its pullback followed by the derived counit. Since t-exact functors carry truncation triangles to truncation triangles, uniqueness in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] shows that $f^*$ commutes with both truncations and their canonical maps. The induced functor on hearts is exact, because short exact sequences of hearts are precisely distinguished triangles of heart objects in that same cited statement.

source.place: XVII Proposition 5.2.2(b), with the representing Hom bijections

proof.text: We verify the derived counit $f^*Rf_*L\to L$ itself. All morphisms from a Noetherian scheme are quasi-compact and quasi-separated: preimages of affine opens are quasi-compact opens, and the inverse image of an affine open under the diagonal is an open of the Noetherian source. Thus [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] applies. At $\bar y$, [lem-per-pseudo-open-strict-local-fibre] identifies its right-hand side with $R\Gamma(Y_{(\bar y)},L|_{Y_{(\bar y)}})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk], global sections there are the closed geometric stalk, an exact functor, so these derived sections are $L_{\bar y}$. The restriction/germ map in the stalk formula is the counit on this stalk. The formula is valid for module coefficients by [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients], and stalk conservativity [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] proves that the derived counit is an isomorphism. Pullback commutes with truncations by Step 5, so its upper truncation proves $f^*f_*^pL\cong L$. For heart objects $L,N$ the adjunction now identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(f_*^pL,f_*^pN)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(L,N)$, proving full faithfulness.

source.place: XVII Proposition 5.2.2(c); Stacks 03Q9, theorem-higher-direct-images, for the derived counit test

proof.text: For composable pseudo-open $g:Z\to Y$ and $f:Y\to X$, inverse-image composition [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] gives $(fg)^*\cong g^*f^*$, also on the hearts. Both $(fg)_*^p$ and $f_*^pg_*^{p\circ f}$ represent the resulting right-adjoint Hom functor. The unique right-adjoint comparison [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] gives their canonical isomorphism. Its unit and counit are the pasted ones by the last clause of that cited statement. Consequently all the identifications respect the specified heart adjunction maps; no unnormalized choice of an isomorphism is being made.

source.place: XVII Proposition 5.2.2(d) and its adjunction proof

proof.text: For etale restriction, localization, and strict localization $h:Y\to X$, the map is locally ind-etale. In the localization case [lem-weil-pbc-localization-colimit-principal-localizations] expresses it as a filtered limit of principal open immersions, which are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. In the strict-local case use [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-affine-chart-ind-etale]; the etale case is a constant diagram. The strict localizations at corresponding geometric points are canonically isomorphic by [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance]. Exactness and stalk compatibility from [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] give the upper vanishing condition. The costalk definition of [lem-per-supported-generators-costalk-detection], applied on those identical pointed strict local schemes, gives the lower one. Thus $h^*$ is t-exact for the pulled-back function and commutes with truncation by the uniqueness argument of Step 5.

source.place: XVII 5.2 and the strict-local first reduction in proof of 5.3.1(a)

proof.text: For any quasi-compact quasi-separated $j:W\to X$, form its base-change $j_Y:W_Y\to Y$ along one of the maps $h$ in Step 8. The ordinary exchange $h^*Rj_*\to Rj_{Y,*}h_W^*$ is an isomorphism: at $\bar y\to Y$, the two strict-local stalk formulas of [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] are derived sections over $W\times_XX_{(h\bar y)}$ and $W_Y\times_YY_{(\bar y)}$. These are the same pointed base change by [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance]; the exchange is restriction along that canonical isomorphism. Module coefficients and the actual mate are identified by [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients], and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] concludes. Apply this with the generic inclusion $j:\eta\to X$, which is quasi-compact and separated: inverse images of affine opens are either empty or the one affine point, and the diagonal is the identity. Combining exchange with Step 8's truncation comparison gives $h^*\tau_{\leq p}Rj_*\cong\tau_{\leq p\circ h}Rj_{Y,*}h_\eta^*$, with the comparison to the derived pushforward unchanged.

source.place: XVII first reduction of proof 5.3.1(a); Stacks 03Q9, theorem-higher-direct-images, applied on both sides of exchange

proof.text: Here is why the base-changed generic scheme in Step 9 has the claimed componentwise meaning. For etale $Y\to X$ with $X$ normal integral, [lem-fin-etale-normal-components] decomposes $Y$ into finitely many open-and-closed normal integral components. For a localization or strict localization, the ring is a local filtered colimit of etale algebras over a normal domain; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain] makes it a normal domain and makes the base map injective. On an affine normal integral component $\operatorname{Spec}B$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. For an etale component the same local-colimit lemma applied at any point proves $A\to B_y$ injective, and hence $A\to B$ injective. The generic fibre ring $K\otimes_AB$ is nonzero (the base is injective) and a domain (it is a localization of $B$). It is ind-etale over $K$; this follows from [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. By [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field], each element lies in a finite etale $K$-subalgebra. Inside a domain such a finite-dimensional subalgebra is a field: multiplication by any nonzero element is injective and hence surjective on the finite-dimensional vector space. Thus $K\otimes_AB$ is a field. Since it is obtained by localizing $B$, it is its fraction field. This identifies $\eta\times_XY$ with the generic points of the components. On each such point $h_\eta^*$ preserves the ordinary shifted heart, so the heart extension in Step 9 is defined.

source.place: XVII 5.3.1(a), strict-local reduction of generic extension, with the normal integral components made explicit

proof.text: Finally let $X$ be strictly henselian local, $x$ its closed point, $q=p(x)$, and $K=Rg_*L$ for the punctured open $g$. Set $T=\tau^{\mathrm{ord}}_{\leq q}K$ and $C=\tau^{\mathrm{ord}}_{\geq q+1}K$. Ordinary truncation gives $T\to K\to C$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Step 6 for the open immersion gives $g^*K\cong L$. Exact restriction and the bound $L\in D^{\mathrm{ord},\leq q}$ show $g^*T\cong L$ and $g^*C=0$. Thus $C$ is supported at $x$. The support equivalence follows degreewise from [lem-kun-04ca]; closed pushforward is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] and [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact], so this identifies $C=i_*V$ with $V\in D^{\mathrm{ord},\geq q+1}(x_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. These identifications are linear since all kernel and counit maps are linear. The supported-kernel definition [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel] gives $i^!i_*V=V$: $i_*$ preserves injectives by [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], since its exact left adjoint is $i^*$, and the underived supported kernel on $i_*V$ is all of $i_*V$. Hence $C\in D^{\geq p+1}$, since away from $x$ its costalks vanish and at $x$ its costalk is $V$.

source.place: XVII proof of 5.3.1(a), equality with ordinary truncation, support at the closed point

proof.text: The object $T$ is in $D^{\leq p}$: on $U$ it is $L$ and at $x$ its ordinary stalk has degrees at most $q$. It also belongs to $D^{\geq p}$. Indeed the closed-support triangle [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle], applied to $K=Rg_*L$, has its middle map an isomorphism, by the derived adjunction counit and its triangle identity from Step 6. Thus $i_*i^!K=0$. The right derived supported kernel carries triangles to triangles by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Applying it to $T\to K\to C$ consequently gives $i^!T\cong V[-1]$, of degrees at least $q+2$; this is stronger than the required lower bound $q$. On $U$ the lower bound is that of $L$. The triangle $T\to K\to C$ therefore has its first object in the heart and its last object in $D^{\geq p+1}$. Uniqueness of the perverse truncation triangle [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] identifies $T$ with $\tau_{\leq p}K=g_*^pL$, and identifies the arrow $T\to K$ with the perverse-truncation arrow. Its restriction to $U$ is the given counit $g^*K\to L$. This proves both compatibility assertions in the last clause.
